full_judgment:
5. Being aggrieved he filed writ petition No.665 of 2011 before the High Court Division. Rule Nisi was issued. Besides, earlier CPLA No.1220 of 2009 has also been dismissed on 13-6-2013. Ultimately upon hearing the Rule was discharged on 27-11-2016 directing him to seek relief before the Administrative Tribunal by resorting to section 14/29 of the Limitation Act, 1908. Meanwhile he also preferred departmental Appeal to opposite party No.1, the Secretary, Ministry of Civil Aviation and tourism, Bangladesh on 12-1-2017. The departmental appeal not being disposed of within two months he constrained to file AT Case as aforementioned. 

 11. He further submits that earlier it was observed by the High Court Division in the Judgment and Order dated 27-12-2016 passed in Writ Petition No. 665 of 2011 that the petitioner's (respondent No. 1 of the instant civil petition) approach to file instant AT Case No. 93 of 2017 shall be subject to applicability of section 14 read with section 29 of the Limitation Act, 1908 which, in fact, is not applicable alongside the Administrative. Tribunal Act, 1980. Without considering the same learned Appellate Tribunal below most illegally observed that the AT Case is well within time in pursuance of the condonation of delay under section 14 of the Limitation Act and as such the same is liable to be set-aside. 

 12. He further submits that earlier the High Court Division in the Judgment and Order dated 27-12-2016 passed in Writ Petition No. 665 of 2011 discharged the rule with observation that the writ petitioner (respondent No. 1 of the instant civil petition) shall be at liberty to approach the Administrative Tribunal subject to satisfying the question of limitation, by resorting to section 14 read with section 29 of the Limitation Act, 1908 if the same are applicable. The petitioner (respondent No. 1 of the instant civil petition) filed AT Case No 93 of 2017 before the Administrative Tribunal No. 1, Dhaka, on 20-3-2017, almost after 4 months of the order of the High Court Division without giving any cogent ground for such delay. The opposite party of the AT Case No. 93 of 2017 clearly stated in their written objection that the case is barred by limitation. However, the learned Administrative Appellate Tribunal, without considering this aspect most illegally observed that the AT Case No. 93 of 2017 filed by the petitioner on 20-3-2017 is well within time and that the opposite party did not raise any objection to that effect before the Tribunal below and as such the impugned judgment and order dated 22-11-2021 passed by the learned Administrative Appellate Tribunal in AAT Appeal No. 267 of 2018 is liable to be set-aside. 

 16. On appreciation of the argument of the parties it is felt by us that the core question that has to be addressed in this Civil petition is that whether the case filed before the Administrative Tribunal is barred by limitation and whether the order of dismissal from service of the respondent No. 1 is sustainable under the law. 

 22. It is true that subsequently writ petition No. 665 of 2011 was discharged on the point of maintainability holding that if any government servant h.is any grievance with regarded to his service related matter he may invoke the forum as provided in Article 117 of the Constitution through challenging the respondents action/ decision before the Administrative Tribunal. Hence, the petitioner shall be at liberty to approach the Administrative Tribunal subject to satisfying the question of limitation, by resorting to section 14 read with section 29 of the Limitation act, 1908 if the same are applicable. 

 "14. (1) In computing the period of limitation prescribed for any suit, the time during which the plaintiff has been prosecuting with due diligence another civil proceeding, whether in a Court of first instance or in a Court of appeal, against the defendant, shall be excluded, where the proceeding is founded upon the same cause of action and is prosecuted in good faith in a Court which, from defect of jurisdiction, or other cause of a like nature, is unable to entertain it. 

 (2) In computing the period of limitation prescribed for any application, the time during which the applicant has been prosecuting with due diligence another civil proceeding, whether in a Court of first instance or in a Court of appeal, against the same party for the same relief shall be excluded, where such proceeding is prosecuted in good faith in a Court which, from defect of jurisdiction, or other cause of a like nature, is unable to entertain it." 

 "We make it clear that if the writ petitioners desire to redress their grievances before the Administrative Tribunal since they had been prosecuting their grievances in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh for a long time, the Administrative Tribunal shall entertain their petitions, if any, are filed on condoning the delay under section 14 of the limitation Act. We also waive the statutory bar applicable to an applicant for filling a departmental appeal before the appellate authority, since they have already moved the High Court Division, the said period of limitation has already expired. We want to make it clear that the provision to sub section (4) shall not stand in the way in making the applications and the Administrative Tribunal shall admit the petitions as if the applicants have preferred appeals under proviso to sub section(4)". 

 25. It further appears that subsequent writ petition No. 665 of 2011 was filed on 20-1-2011 and it was discharged on 27-11-2016 and compliance of 1st proviso under section 6 (2) of the Act, 1980 on 12-1-2017, the AT Case was filed on 20-3-2017. Therefore, it is well within time in pursuance of the condonation of delay under section 14 of the Limitation Act for prosecuting in a wrong forum. 

 27. In view of the above discussion it is abundantly clear that the case filed before the Administrative Tribunal is not barred by limitation. It is also established that no fraud was practiced on the part of the respondent No. 1 as alleged by the authority (CAAB) in obtaining his appointment. The authority absolutely dealt the respondent No.1 roughly and wrongly. The learned Judge of the Administrative Appellate Tribunal rightly affirmed the judgment of the Administrative Tribunal awarding him relief by the impugned judgment and order.
